# System context
You are part of a multi-agent system called the Agents SDK, designed to make agent coordination and execution easy. Agents uses two primary abstraction: **Agents** and **Handoffs**. An agent encompasses instructions and tools and can hand off a conversation to another agent when appropriate. Handoffs are achieved by calling a handoff function, generally named `transfer_to_<agent_name>`. Transfers between agents are handled seamlessly in the background; do not mention or draw attention to these transfers in your conversation with the user.


Tu es un rédacteur spécialisé. Tu rédiges UN SEUL chapitre d'un rapport de recherche, jamais le rapport entier. D'autres rédacteurs s'occupent des autres chapitres en parallèle.

On te fournit :
- le titre du rapport (pour le contexte),
- le titre et l'objectif de TON chapitre,
- les sources prioritaires pour ce chapitre,
- le corpus complet des sources, chaque source préfixée par son identifiant `[S#]`.

Règles :
- N'utilise QUE l'information présente dans le corpus fourni — aucune connaissance externe. Si une information manque, ne l'invente pas.
- Concentre-toi sur l'objectif de ton chapitre. Tu peux puiser dans n'importe quelle source du corpus, pas seulement les prioritaires, si cela sert ton objectif.
- Cite tes sources inline avec leur identifiant, par exemple `[S2]`. Chaque affirmation importante doit être traçable à au moins une source. C'est ce qui rend le rapport vérifiable.
- Commence directement par le contenu en markdown. Ne répète pas le titre du chapitre : il sera ajouté automatiquement lors de l'assemblage.
- N'enveloppe PAS ta réponse dans un bloc de code (pas de ``` ni de ```markdown autour du texte) : écris le markdown directement, il est inséré tel quel dans le rapport.
- Ne rédige pas l'introduction ni la conclusion générale du rapport : ce n'est pas ton rôle, et cela créerait des redondances avec les autres chapitres.
- Reste factuel et concis. Développe les idées utiles, sans remplissage.

Réponds uniquement avec le texte markdown de ton chapitre.

Titre du rapport : FY2025 AI Capex Intensity Data Pack — Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Apple
Chapitre à rédiger : Data Gaps
Objectif du chapitre : Identify any missing required FY2025 actual metrics per company and state that Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Apple guidance is unavailable; do not infer missing values.
Sources prioritaires : S7, S1

Corpus complet (cite avec [S#]) :

### [S1] frozen fy2025 initial capex guidance release date basis amazon 100b alphabet 75b meta 60 65b finance lease principal microsoft nvidia apple guidance unavailable forward looking
(source: frozen_fy2025_initial_capex_guidance_release_date_basis_amazon_100b_alphabet_75b_meta_60_65b_finance_lease_principal_microsoft_nvidia_apple_guidance_unavailable_forward_looking.txt)

The frozen initial FY2025 capex guidance (snapshot as of February 7, 2025) records the first full-year 2025 guidance available after each company's FY2024 results; it is a historical snapshot and later revisions must not be substituted, with guidance remaining forward-looking and separate from reported FY2025 actuals [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:0][doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:1].

The frozen figures, release dates, and bases are: Amazon released guidance on 2025-02-06 of approximately $100B, based on management's estimate of capital expenditures; Alphabet released guidance on 2025-02-04 of approximately $75B, based on reported capex (with cash-payment timing causing variability); and Meta released guidance on 2025-01-29 of $60B–$65B, a basis that includes principal payments on finance leases [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:1]. For Meta specifically, the corpus actual is cash paid to acquire property and equipment and excludes finance-lease principal, so a percentage variance against Meta's guidance is not like-for-like and must not be calculated; the FY2025 company-reported capex including finance-lease principal was $72.215B ($69.691B cash PP&E plus $2.524B finance-lease principal) [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:2].

No initial FY2025 capex guidance is provided in the frozen source pack for Microsoft, NVIDIA, or Apple; this should be reported as unavailable rather than estimated [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:2]. Primary releases were used to validate this frozen source [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:2].

### [S2] fy2025 fiscal year end definitions amazon december alphabet december meta december microsoft june nvidia late january apple late september revenue operating income operating margin ocf capex fcf definitions sec 10k usd billions
(source: fy2025_fiscal_year_end_definitions_amazon_december_alphabet_december_meta_december_microsoft_june_nvidia_late_january_apple_late_september_revenue_operating_income_operating_margin_ocf_capex_fcf_definitions_sec_10k_usd_billions.txt)

The six companies use differing fiscal year ends (FYE), so FY2025 periods must be compared on a fiscal-year basis, not a calendar basis. Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta end their fiscal years in December; Microsoft in June; NVIDIA in late January; and Apple in late September [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0]. All figures are sourced from each company's SEC Form 10-K consolidated statements and reported in US$ billions [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0][doc_key_metrics.csv.md:0].

Metric definitions: Operating margin = Operating income / Revenue; Free cash flow (FCF) = Operating cash flow − Capex; Capex intensity = Capex / Operating cash flow [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0].

FY2025 headline figures: Amazon (Dec) revenue $716.9B, operating margin 11.2%, OCF $139.5B, capex $131.8B, FCF $7.7B, capex/OCF 94% [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:2]. Alphabet (Dec) revenue $402.8B, margin 32.0%, OCF $164.7B, capex $91.4B, FCF $73.3B, capex/OCF 56% [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:5]. Meta (Dec) revenue $201.0B, margin 41.4%, OCF $115.8B, capex $69.7B, FCF $46.1B, capex/OCF 60% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:3].

Microsoft (Jun) FY2025: revenue $281.7B, margin 45.6%, OCF $136.2B, capex $64.6B, FCF $71.6B, capex/OCF 47% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:4]. NVIDIA (Jan) FY2025: revenue $130.5B, margin 62.4%, OCF $64.1B, capex $3.2B, FCF $60.9B, capex/OCF 5% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:5]. Apple (Sep) FY2025 data were not present in the retrieved chunks; Apple figures should be treated as unavailable rather than estimated [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:3].

### [S3] fy2025 operating cash flow capex free cash flow capex-to-ocf ratio capex intensity amazon alphabet meta microsoft nvidia apple fiscal year figures
(source: fy2025_operating_cash_flow_capex_free_cash_flow_capex-to-ocf_ratio_capex_intensity_amazon_alphabet_meta_microsoft_nvidia_apple_fiscal_year_figures.txt)

FY2025 cash generation and capex metrics (US$ billions) for the six companies, per fiscal-year-end (FYE): Amazon/Alphabet/Meta = Dec; Microsoft = Jun; NVIDIA = Jan; Apple = Sep. FCF = OCF − capex; capex intensity = capex/OCF [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0].

- **Amazon (FY2025):** OCF $139.5B, capex $131.8B, FCF $7.7B, capex/OCF 94% (up from $40.1B capex in FY2020) [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2].
- **Alphabet (FY2025):** OCF $164.7B, capex $91.4B, FCF $73.3B, capex/OCF 56% (capex rose from $22.3B in FY2020) [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2].
- **Meta (FY2025):** OCF $115.8B, capex $69.7B, FCF $46.1B, capex/OCF 60% (capex rose from $15.2B in FY2020) [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:3].
- **Microsoft (FY2025):** OCF $136.2B, capex $64.6B, FCF $71.6B, capex/OCF 47% (up from $15.4B in FY2020) [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:4].
- **NVIDIA (FY2025):** OCF $64.1B, capex $3.2B, FCF $60.9B, capex/OCF 5% (capex moved from $1.0B in FY2022) [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:5].
- **Apple (FY2025):** OCF $111.5B, capex $12.7B, FCF $98.8B, capex/OCF 11% (capex moved from $7.3B in FY2020) [doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:3].

Capex intensity is highest at Amazon (94%), followed by Meta (60%) and Alphabet (56%), reflecting heavy AI/data-center investment, while NVIDIA (5%) and Apple (11%) remain capital-light with high cash conversion [doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:1]. Microsoft sits mid-range at 47% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:4]. Figures are consistent across the CSV and reference datasets (e.g., key_metrics.csv.md confirms Microsoft FY2025 OCF $136.2B, capex $64.6B, FCF $71.6B, capex/OCF 47%) [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:11].

### [S4] fy2025 revenue operating income operating margin amazon alphabet meta microsoft nvidia apple in usd billions from fiscal year financial statements
(source: fy2025_revenue_operating_income_operating_margin_amazon_alphabet_meta_microsoft_nvidia_apple_in_usd_billions_from_fiscal_year_financial_statements.txt)

FY2025 profitability profile for the six companies, all figures in US$ billions (operating margin in percent). Fiscal-year-ends differ by company: Amazon/Alphabet/Meta = December; Microsoft = June; NVIDIA = late January; Apple = late September, so comparisons are on a fiscal-year basis [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0].

- **NVIDIA** (FYE Jan): Revenue $130.5B, Operating income $81.5B, Operating margin 62.4% — the highest margin of the group [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:11][doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:5].
- **Microsoft** (FYE Jun): Revenue $281.7B, Operating income $128.5B, Operating margin 45.6% [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:11][doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:4].
- **Meta** (FYE Dec): Revenue $201.0B, Operating income $83.3B, Operating margin 41.4% [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:5][doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:3].
- **Alphabet** (FYE Dec): Revenue $402.8B, Operating income $129.0B, Operating margin 32.0% [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:5][doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2].
- **Apple** (FYE Sep): Revenue $416.2B, Operating income $133.1B, Operating margin 32.0% [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:16][doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:6].
- **Amazon** (FYE Dec): Revenue $716.9B, Operating income $80.0B, Operating margin 11.2% — the lowest margin, on the largest revenue base [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:2][doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2].

Amazon leads in absolute revenue ($716.9B) but trails in profitability, while NVIDIA generates the highest operating margin (62.4%) despite the smallest revenue. Microsoft, Meta, and NVIDIA all exceed 41% operating margin, versus roughly 32% for Alphabet and Apple and 11% for Amazon [doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:1][doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:3]. In absolute operating income, Apple leads ($133.1B), closely followed by Alphabet ($129.0B) and Microsoft ($128.5B).

### [S5] capex trend fy2020 to fy2025 growth
(source: capex_trend_fy2020_to_fy2025_growth.txt)

Capex trajectories from earliest reported fiscal year through FY2025 (US$B):

- **Amazon (FYE Dec):** FY2020 $40.1B → FY2025 $131.8B; ~3.3x increase. Capex/OCF rose from 61% to 94% [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:0][Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data:2][Analyst_Prep_Notes:1].
- **Alphabet (FYE Dec):** FY2020 $22.3B → FY2025 $91.4B; ~4.1x increase. Capex/OCF climbed from 34% to 56% [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:5][Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data:2][Analyst_Prep_Notes:1].
- **Meta (FYE Dec):** FY2020 $15.2B → FY2025 $69.7B; ~4.6x increase. Capex/OCF rose to 60% [Analyst_Prep_Notes:1][Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data:4].
- **Microsoft (FYE Jun):** FY2020 $15.4B → FY2025 $64.6B; ~4.2x increase. Capex/OCF rose from 25% to 47% [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:9][Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data:4][Analyst_Prep_Notes:2].
- **NVIDIA (FYE Jan):** earliest reported capex is FY2022 at $1.0B → FY2025 $3.2B; ~3.2x increase. Capex/OCF remained low (~5%), reflecting its asset-light model [Analyst_Prep_Notes:2][doc_key_metrics.csv.md:11].
- **Apple (FYE Sep):** FY2020 $7.3B → FY2025 $12.7B; ~1.7x increase. Capex/OCF held low at ~11% [Analyst_Prep_Notes:3][doc_key_metrics.csv.md:16].

Magnitude and direction: five of six companies (all but Apple) showed large, accelerating capex growth, with Alphabet, Meta, and Microsoft roughly quadrupling spend from FY2020 to FY2025, and Amazon tripling — driven by AI/data-center buildout. Apple's capex grew least in both absolute and relative terms (~1.7x), keeping it structurally distinct. NVIDIA's absolute spend is smallest but tripled over FY2022–FY2025. Initial FY2025 guidance for Amazon (~$100B), Alphabet (~$75B), and Meta ($60–65B) indicates investment momentum continued into the reported year [Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance:1]. Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Apple had no initial FY2025 capex guidance in the frozen source [Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance:2]. Fiscal-year-end basis differs by company (Dec, Jun, Jan, Sep), so figures are compared on a fiscal-year basis [Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data:0].

### [S6] cross-company comparison fy2025
(source: cross-company_comparison_fy2025.txt)

Comparaison consolidée FY2025 — intensité capex, profitabilité et génération de cash (six entreprises)

Les six entreprises ont des fins d'exercice différentes (Amazon/Alphabet/Meta = décembre ; Microsoft = juin ; NVIDIA = fin janvier ; Apple = fin septembre) ; les comparaisons se font sur base fiscale, pas calendaire. Capex intensity = Capex / Operating cash flow ; FCF = OCF − Capex [Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0].

**Amazon** — Revenus $716.9B, marge opérationnelle 11.2%, OCF $139.5B, capex $131.8B, FCF $7.7B, capex/OCF 94% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:1]. L'entreprise la plus intensive en capex (94% de l'OCF), laissant un FCF très faible malgré une génération de cash massive ; le capex a plus que triplé entre FY2020 ($40.1B) et FY2025 [Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:0].

**Alphabet** — Revenus $402.8B, marge op. 32.0%, OCF $164.7B, capex $91.4B, FCF $73.3B, capex/OCF 56% [Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2]. Forte génération de cash avec un FCF élevé, bien que l'intensité capex ait fortement augmenté (42%→56% sur FY2024-FY2025).

**Meta** — Revenus $201.0B, marge op. 41.4%, OCF $115.8B, capex $69.7B, FCF $46.1B, capex/OCF 60% [Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:3]. Marge opérationnelle élevée avec un niveau de capex/OCF en hausse (41%→60%).

**Microsoft** — Revenus $281.7B, marge op. 45.6%, OCF $136.2B, capex $64.6B, FCF $71.6B, capex/OCF 47% [Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:4]. Meilleure marge opérationnelle du groupe (45.6%) avec un FCF solide, mais une intensité capex en forte progression (38%→47%).

**NVIDIA** — Revenus $130.5B, marge op. 62.4%, OCF $64.1B, capex $3.2B, FCF $60.9B, capex/OCF 5% [Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:5]. Modèle inverse : marge opérationnelle la plus élevée et la plus faible intensité capex (5%), convertissant presque tout l'OCF en FCF.

**Apple** — Revenus $416.2B, marge op. 32.0%, OCF $111.5B, capex $12.7B, FCF $98.8B, capex/OCF 11% [Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:3]. Très faible intensité capex (11%) et FCF élevé, comparable à NVIDIA en termes de conversion du cash.

**Synthèse** — Spectre opposé d'intensité capex : Amazon (94%) et Meta (60%) en tête, Microsoft (47%) et Alphabet (56%) intermédiaires, Apple (11%) et NVIDIA (5%) très faibles. En termes de profitabilité, NVIDIA (62.4%) et Microsoft (45.6%) dominent, suivis de Meta (41.4%) ; Alphabet et Apple (32%) intermédiaires, Amazon (11.2%) nettement plus faible. La génération de FCF est la plus forte chez Apple ($98.8B) et Alphabet ($73.3B), la plus faible chez Amazon ($7.7B) malgré le plus gros OCF ($139.5B) [Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:1][Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:3].

### [S7] missing unavailable not disclosed fy2025 actual metrics revenue operating income margin ocf capex fcf per company microsoft nvidia apple capex guidance unavailable data gaps
(source: missing_unavailable_not_disclosed_fy2025_actual_metrics_revenue_operating_income_margin_ocf_capex_fcf_per_company_microsoft_nvidia_apple_capex_guidance_unavailable_data_gaps.txt)

## FY2025 Actual Metrics Availability by Company

All six companies have complete FY2025 actual metrics (revenue, operating income, operating margin, operating cash flow, capex, FCF) in the corpus. Amazon: revenue $716.9B, operating margin 11.2%, OCF $139.5B, capex $131.8B, FCF $7.7B [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:1]; Alphabet: revenue $402.8B, margin 32.0%, OCF $164.7B, capex $91.4B, FCF $73.3B [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2]; Meta: revenue $201.0B, margin 41.4%, OCF $115.8B, capex $69.7B, FCF $46.1B [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:3]; Microsoft: revenue $281.7B, margin 45.6%, OCF $136.2B, capex $64.6B, FCF $71.6B [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:4]; NVIDIA: revenue $130.5B, margin 62.4%, OCF $64.1B, capex $3.2B, FCF $60.9B [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:5]; Apple: revenue $416.2B, margin 32.0%, OCF $111.5B, capex $12.7B, FCF $98.8B [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:6].

## Unavailable Capex Guidance (Key Data Gap)

No initial FY2025 capex guidance is provided in the frozen source pack for **Microsoft, NVIDIA, or Apple**; these must be reported as unavailable rather than estimated [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:2]. Guidance exists only for Amazon (~$100B, released 2025-02-06), Alphabet (~$75B, released 2025-02-04), and Meta ($60B-$65B, released 2025-01-29) [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:1]. Guidance is forward-looking and must remain separate from reported FY2025 actuals; later revisions must not be substituted [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:0].

## Additional Data Gaps and Comparability Issues

NVIDIA has no capex, FCF, or capex/OCF figures for FY2020 and FY2021 (marked "None" in the source) [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:5]. For Meta, the corpus actual (cash PP&E, $69.691B) excludes finance-lease principal, so a percentage variance against Meta's guidance is not like-for-like and must not be calculated; the company-reported measure including finance-lease principal was $72.215B [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:2]. Fiscal-year-end differs by company (Dec for Amazon/Alphabet/Meta, Jun for Microsoft, late Jan for NVIDIA, late Sep for Apple), so comparisons must be on a fiscal-year basis [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0].
